lessons.title: What it means for a machine to learn
lessons.outcome: You can say what it means for a machine to learn. You fit a line by hand, then let the computer fit it, and test both lines on new points.

lessons.title: The gradient
lessons.outcome: You can find how much the loss changes when one weight changes a little. This number is the gradient, and it tells you which way to move the weight.

lessons.title: Using the gradient
lessons.outcome: You can explain how gradient descent changes two weights at the same time. You can also say why a learning rate that is too large makes the loss grow.
lessons.code:
optim::SGD opt({&W, &b}, /*lr=*/0.05f);
loss.backward();   // fills W.grad, b.grad
opt.step();        // W -= lr * W.grad, same for b
opt.zero_grad();   // clear before the next backward

lessons.title: Layers
lessons.outcome: You can calculate the output of one neuron from its inputs and weights. You can explain why a layer of many neurons is one matrix product.
lessons.code:
nn::Linear layer(784, 32);   // W (32, 784), b (32)
Variable y = layer(x);       // x (B, 784) → y (B, 32)

lessons.title: Nonlinearity
lessons.outcome: You can explain why two layers without an activation function act like one layer. You can see how ReLU units bend a straight line into a curve.
lessons.code:
Variable h = relu(z);                 // max(0, z)
Variable s = sigmoid(z);              // 1 / (1 + e^-z)
Variable p = softmax(z, /*axis=*/1);  // each row sums to 1

lessons.title: Two classes and the line between them
lessons.outcome: You can explain how a network sorts points into two classes. You can see how more hidden units bend the line between the classes.

lessons.title: Losses
lessons.outcome: You can turn the scores of a network into probabilities with softmax. You can explain why cross-entropy is a better loss than squared error for classes.
lessons.code:
nn::MSELoss mse;                      // regression
nn::CrossEntropyLoss ce;              // classification
Variable loss = ce(logits, labels);   // logits (B, 10), labels (B)

lessons.title: How the computer finds every gradient at once
lessons.outcome: You can explain why it is too slow to find each gradient by changing one weight at a time. You can follow the chain rule backward through a small network.

lessons.title: Why deep networks are hard to start
lessons.outcome: You can explain why the gradients can become very small in a deep network. You can also say why the start values of the weights are important.

lessons.title: The training loop
lessons.outcome: You can explain why training uses small groups of examples, called batches. You can follow the five lines of the training loop in TorC.

lessons.title: Better optimizers
lessons.outcome: You can compare momentum, Adam and AdamW on the same problem. You can say how each of them changes the size of a step.

lessons.title: Generalization
lessons.outcome: You can tell when a model only memorizes its training data. You can use a separate set of data to choose when to stop training.

lessons.title: Digits with an MLP
lessons.outcome: You can train a network that reads handwritten digits and count its mistakes. You can say which digits it mixes up, and why.

lessons.title: One training step from start to end
lessons.outcome: You can follow one training step on one digit, from the pixels to the changed weight. You see the probability of the right digit go up.

lessons.title: Convolution
lessons.outcome: You can explain how a small pattern detector slides over an image. You can count the weights of a convolution layer and find the size of its output.

lessons.title: Digits with a CNN
lessons.outcome: You can explain why a convolutional network reads the same digits with fewer weights than the first network for digits.

lessons.title: From digits to ChatGPT
lessons.outcome: You can explain how ChatGPT learns to predict the next word with the same loop as this course. You know where TorC stops and where to learn more.

lessons.title: Tensors
lessons.outcome: You can read the shape of a tensor in TorC. You can predict the result of broadcasting, of a sum along an axis and of a batched matrix product.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.outcome: You can build a TorC model from Module and Sequential. You can list its parameters and explain the rule for the forward cache.

lessons.title: Common errors in TorC programs
lessons.outcome: You can find the cause of the most common errors in TorC programs. You can read the error messages that TorC gives.

lessons.title: The symbols of this course
lessons.outcome: You can look up each symbol of this course, with its name and the lesson that introduces it.

lessons.title: Glossary
lessons.outcome: You can look up each term of this course, with a short definition in plain words.

lessons.title: Backprop lab
lessons.outcome: You can run small calculations forward and backward, and see where each gradient comes from.
